comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete pinned manifest (SHA-256 ee9985787565dc1746699aec8f77b688f6e04c2836d04f12467e3f8e0a076dd7): 135 files selected from all LIBERO BDDL definitions, benchmark registries, and predicate implementations at commit 8f1084e3132a39270c3a13ebe37270a43ece2a01. Searched the complete manifest inventory by the candidate’s mechanisms—rail, slide, drawer, transfer, insertion, block, carriage, bearing, and balls—then read the complete closest original BDDL definition. The inventory was used only for navigation; the verdict relies on the original file.
comparisons.objective: The candidate transfers an uncaged recirculating-ball LM block from a service rail to a physically butted jig while preserving every rolling element. The closest LIBERO objective merely opens a cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: bimanual end-face mating, parallel-axis alignment, continuous support across a rail-to-jig boundary, force-limited block sliding, alignment-preserving regrasping, and containment of free balls. LIBERO neighbor: actuate one articulated drawer until its Open predicate holds.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success requires complete transfer, physical rail/jig contact, maintained parallelism, all balls retained in four circulating rows, no gap, jam, impact, contamination, or unsafe inclination, followed by a stable release. LIBERO success is only `(Open wooden_cabinet_1_top_region)`.

closest_tasks.name: open the top drawer of the cabinet
closest_tasks.quote: (:language open the top drawer of the cabinet)
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Grasp and translate an already supported prismatic drawer.
closest_tasks.reason: Both involve constrained linear motion, but the LIBERO drawer remains continuously supported by its own articulation. It does not require mating two separate supports, transferring a carriage across their interface, bimanual alignment, or retaining free rolling elements.

comparisons.reason: No inspected LIBERO definition tests continuous support transfer of an uncaged bearing carriage. The nearest shared primitive—linear sliding—is insufficient to establish the same objective, mechanism, or failure-sensitive ability.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete pinned manifest (SHA-256 7a3cf904dfb3437135ca2002172c2d8fcced2531e13a2d4a6a3ca3185030d545): 381 files covering kitchen environment definitions, the environment registry, and dataset registry at commit 425684d332f135f5b30a40b321f52d15a0fe9250. Searched every inventory entry for rail/slide/rack/drawer/transfer/insertion/bearing mechanisms and read the complete original `kitchen_oven.py` containing the closest rack task.
comparisons.objective: The candidate moves an uncaged LM block between two separately positioned supports without losing balls. RoboCasa’s closest task slides an oven rack inward or outward while it remains part of the oven fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: bimanual jig-to-rail alignment plus force-limited transfer over a potentially discontinuous interface. RoboCasa: unimanual translation of a supported oven rack along its existing guides.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success jointly gates full transfer, contact and parallelism of the supports, preservation of every ball, prohibited-contact avoidance, and hands-off stability. SlideOvenRack checks only normalized rack position: at least 0.95 when pulled out or at most 0.05 when pushed in.

closest_tasks.name: SlideOvenRack
closest_tasks.quote: ep_meta["lang"] = f"Fully slide the oven rack {direction}."
closest_tasks.objective: Fully slide an oven rack in or out.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Translate a rack constrained by an existing oven guide.
closest_tasks.success_condition: `return current_pos >= 0.95` for pulling or `return current_pos <= 0.05` for pushing.
closest_tasks.reason: The task shares guided sliding but not support-interface construction, bimanual parallel alignment, carriage handoff, regrasping while maintaining support, or free-element containment.

comparisons.reason: Across the complete RoboCasa registry, rack and drawer tasks retain their original guide support and score fixture state. They do not test the candidate’s essential rail-to-jig handoff mechanism or rolling-element-loss failure.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 11 pinned definition and registration files in the complete manifest (SHA-256 81f679c8aa727b08fc32b1830972b993cb4705e1bed8ce13da1ede4ec8a1da60): 2 SimplerEnv registry/builder files at commit eddb5690749a1e34267807c0f7b5eede323918d7 and 9 ManiSkill2-real2sim environment files at commit ef7a4d4fdf4b69f2c2154db5b15b9ac8dfe10682. Searched the complete inventory and read the entire closest drawer environment source.
comparisons.objective: The candidate performs a service transfer of an uncaged bearing block from a rail to a jig. The closest SimplerEnv task opens one cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: coordinated holding of a separate jig, flush/parallel support alignment, controlled carriage translation, and preservation of free balls. SimplerEnv: pull one articulated drawer along a fixed prismatic joint.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete two-component manifest (SHA-256 7ea9b037ea65eb50f79caff9b63b3851fbe438dd48c4119f236b9e1abf03c76d): 1,020 BEHAVIOR-1K files at commit b544acbbb76b461349bcba21f93b870b11da6608 and 101 legacy BDDL activity files at commit 06bec10ca54c7f375a1f71da8b94f7e1896ff77a. Searched all 1,121 inventory entries for mounting, rail, bearing, carriage, insertion, attachment, and sliding tasks. The complete closest current specification was read; no corresponding legacy specification was present in the supplied legacy inventory.
comparisons.objective: The candidate transfers a bearing carriage onto an aligned service jig. BEHAVIOR’s closest semantic neighbor installs a trailer hitch onto a pickup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate explicitly requires bimanual flush alignment, continuous bearing support, force-limited sliding, regrasping, and retention of free balls. The hitch definition exposes only an abstract final `attached` relation and does not specify whether completion entails receiver alignment/insertion, fastening, or another attachment mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success includes full carriage transfer and detailed preservation/failure gates. The hitch task succeeds when the hitch is attached to the pickup.

closest_tasks.name: installing_a_trailer_hitch-0
closest_tasks.objective: Attach a hitch to a pickup.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Potentially align and mount a hitch, but the original BDDL does not encode the physical attachment procedure.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The hitch and pickup satisfy the `attached` predicate.
closest_tasks.reason: The candidate’s rolling-element containment and continuous rail support are absent from the definition. Nevertheless, `attached` is too abstract to determine from this source whether the realized hitch task tests a closely related alignment-and-insertion mechanism. Under the required uncertainty rule, this cannot be called conclusively distinct.

comparisons.reason: The complete registry was covered, but the closest task’s original definition underspecifies its physical mechanism. The candidate has additional explicit abilities, yet the available source cannot rule out meaningful alignment/insertion overlap.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete one-file manifest (SHA-256 641b290bc86e53a147d793c0b52b77f348e656ec768c44c7bab28347ab5c7d31) and read the entire original published-task definition inventory. It enumerates all 10 kept tasks and all 9 considered but excluded tasks, allowing direct coverage of the complete published registry rather than keyword-only sampling.
comparisons.objective: The candidate services a recirculating-ball linear guide by transferring its uncaged carriage onto a mounting/removal jig. The nearest DataCenterBench retained task moves a two-position slider; nearby excluded tasks insert a battery or route a cable into a clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: bimanual precision support mating and controlled carriage handoff while preventing loss of multiple free balls. DataCenterBench’s slider tests a single sliding motion on a fixed control; its connection tasks test ordinary pick-align-push or clip insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success combines full transfer, physical interface continuity, parallelism, all-ball retention, damage/contamination avoidance, and a stable release. The published DataCenterBench description reduces the slider to movement between two fixed positions and states that the tabletop dimmer copies only the sliding motion.

closest_tasks.name: Move a slider
closest_tasks.quote: Real UPS mode selector has two fixed positions. Our dimmer copies only the sliding motion.
closest_tasks.objective: Move a tabletop slider corresponding to a UPS mode selector.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Translate a fixed slider between two positions.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Reach the requested fixed selector position; the published definition does not add interface-alignment or containment gates.
closest_tasks.reason: The only commonality is linear motion. The slider is already constrained and does not require transferring a carriage between supports or preserving rolling elements.

closest_tasks.name: Press a cable into a clip
closest_tasks.quote: Real step routes cables along a switch tray. Ours uses one clip.
closest_tasks.objective: Seat a cable in a routing clip.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Align and press a deformable cable into one fixed clip.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Cable is retained by the clip.
closest_tasks.reason: This has alignment and retention, but neither a moving carriage nor a continuous rigid support handoff, recirculating free elements, parallel rail mating, or bimanual gap control.

comparisons.reason: The complete published registry consists of controls, connectors, clipping, key turning, and excluded elementary service steps. None tests continuous support transfer of an uncaged bearing carriage or loss prevention for its rolling elements.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified the complete pinned manifest (SHA-256 bb423627a3d3ef68b8e6a9441309f1f8444644cac785ac082b2eba0eb3f9b128): all 110 selected task implementations, YAML configurations, and task-registry files at commit f57e1633ffed59761bc8e568cfe7530c4b33381c. Searched the complete inventory for ball, tube, insertion, rail, alignment, transfer, and containment mechanisms, then read both complete task/config pairs for the two closest candidates.
comparisons.objective: The candidate moves a recirculating-ball bearing block between a rail and a service jig without losing any ball. `pour_balls_into_vase` transfers seven loose balls between open containers; `insert_tubes` places three tubes individually into a rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: simultaneously hold and align a jig, establish a continuous support path, slide a constrained block across the interface, and preserve balls inside its circulation paths. Pouring requires container transport and tilt; tube insertion requires repeated pick-align-insert actions into independent vertical slots.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires complete block transfer, support contact and parallelism, all balls still contained, prohibited outcomes absent, and stable release. Pouring requires all seven spheres in the vase, the cup upright, and robot return. Tube insertion requires all three tubes inside and sufficiently deep in the slot, within 30 degrees of the required axis, with open grippers.

closest_tasks.name: pour_balls_into_vase
closest_tasks.quote: templates = ["Pour all the balls from the cup into the vase."]
closest_tasks.objective: Pour seven loose balls from a cup into a vase.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Grasp, transport, and tilt a container so free balls enter another container without remaining behind.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each `sphere_0` through `sphere_6` is in the vase, the cup is upright, and all robot arms return to origin.
closest_tasks.reason: Both tasks make the fate of multiple free balls consequential. However, RoboDojo intentionally transfers the balls between containers, whereas the candidate must keep balls inside a moving bearing block while creating and maintaining a continuous rigid support interface. The central tested mechanisms are different.

closest_tasks.name: insert_tubes
closest_tasks.quote: templates = ["Insert the three tubes into the rack one by one."]
closest_tasks.objective: Insert three separate test tubes into a rack.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Repeatedly align and lower rigid tubes into independent rack slots.
closest_tasks.success_condition: All three tubes are in the slot fixture, reach the specified depth, remain within 30 degrees of the required axis, and are released.
closest_tasks.reason: This is genuine precision insertion, but it lacks a carriage already engaged with one guide, a second support that must be held flush and parallel, continuous support during handoff, recirculating balls, and loss-sensitive transfer.

comparisons.reason: The nearest RoboDojo tasks separately cover loose-ball pouring and multi-object insertion, but neither combines them into the candidate’s essential ability: transferring an uncaged bearing carriage across a maintained rail-to-jig interface while its freely simulated rolling elements remain contained.
